# Shard the component test tier across runners, as e2e is

## Context

The `components` job is now the slowest check on every pull request. On #18890's run the test step took 7.0m for 367 tests, and the whole job 7m39s. By comparison `unit` takes about 2.4m and each `e2e-engine` shard about 3m (#18896). @tobiu asked for this ticket: split the tier or run it in parallel.

## The Problem

On `dev` pushes, the step time has followed the test count. The per-test cost has stayed at 1.1 to 1.3 s throughout:

| dev push | tests | test step |
|---|---|---|
| 08-29 | 95 | 1.3m |
| 09-01 | 173 | 3.0m |
| 09-02 | 229 | 4.5m |
| 09-10 | 269 | 5.0m |
| 09-15 | 281 | 5.5m |
| 09-16 | 325 | 6.9m |
| 09-17 | 330 | 7.1m |
| 09-18 (#18890) | 367 | 7.0m |

In #18890's run, the per-test durations add up to 410 s of the 412 s step, so there is no hidden overhead. Each test boots its own harness page, which costs at least 0.36 s (median 0.88 s). The 33 tests that take 2 s or more account for 123 s of the total. Most of the time comes from the number of tests, so trimming fixed waits saves only seconds. The tier also grows with every new component witness.

## The Architectural Reality

- `test/playwright/playwright.config.component.mjs:17-18` sets `fullyParallel: false` and `workers: 1`, both marked `// CRITICAL`. Both have been there since the config's first commit (`1cee840d06`, 2025-10-11), and no reason is recorded.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` has one `test` job over a matrix of `{suite: unit}` and `{suite: components}`.
  - The job's display name is `${{ matrix.suite }}`, and it runs `npm run test-${{ matrix.suite }}`.
  - Every step is gated on `matrix.run`.
  - The failure artifact is named `test-results-${{ matrix.suite }}-${{ github.run_id }}`.
- `dev` has no required status checks, so renaming the check blocks nothing. #18896 relied on the same fact.
- `test/playwright/unit/buildScripts/util/WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` reads `test.yml`'s `changes` job and its `matrix.run` gating.
- `--shard` already splits this suite evenly. The table covers `dev` at 370 tests in 70 files; the times are estimates from #18890's per-file durations:

| split | tests per shard | test time per shard |
|---|---|---|
| 2 shards | 186 · 184 | ~210 s · ~200 s |
| 3 shards | 126 · 134 · 110 | ~122 s · ~153 s · ~134 s |

Each runner also spends about 40 s on setup outside the test step. So two shards finish in about 4.2m and three in about 3.3m.

## The Fix

**Recommended: shard the `components` suite across runners, each still running one worker.** This is the shape #18896 gave e2e.
- Add matrix entries `{suite: components, shard: '1/N'}` and so on, with N = 2 or 3 chosen from the table above.
- The run step passes `--shard=${{ matrix.shard }}` for components only.
- The job name and the artifact name carry the shard.
- `workers: 1` stays, and its `// CRITICAL` comment gets its reason. If none can be found, the PR says so.

**Alternative: parallel workers on one runner** (`workers: 2` in CI). This uses fewer runners, but it changes every test's timing. The component reds that recurred this past week were all timing-sensitive arms: the button menu race, the menu hover-rest arms, and a native drag into an iframe. This path therefore needs a flake measurement before anyone takes it, for example several CI runs at `workers: 2` with no new failure. It is not the default.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1**: on a pull request, the components tier runs as N shards, each `--workers=1`, and the shards' test counts add up to the unsharded `--list` total.
- [ ] **AC-2**: every shard's test step finishes in under 4 minutes on this PR's own CI. The PR body names the slowest shard.
- [ ] **AC-3**: a failing test in any shard fails its check, and the uploaded artifact name includes the shard, so two failing shards do not collide.
- [ ] **AC-4**: `WorkflowScopeClassifier.spec.mjs` stays green, and a push the classifier skips still skips every components shard.
- [ ] **AC-5**: the `// CRITICAL` comment on `workers: 1` states its reason, or the PR records that none was found.

## Out of Scope

- Trimming individual slow arms, such as WorkstationBoot's two ~11 s reload arms.
- Parallel workers within one runner (the alternative above).
- The `DockRailRevealIframe.spec.mjs:221` control-arm flake, which is filed separately.

## Avoided Traps

- ⛔ Treating a higher ceiling as the fix. The ceiling is the time every PR waits.
- ⛔ Sharding by hand-picked spec folders. A hand-made split drifts as new specs land, while `--shard` stays balanced on its own.
- ⛔ Changing the job key or the `matrix.run` gate that the classifier spec reads.
